description: A form flow artifact is valid when all required fields have validation rules, server errors map to user messages, multi-step forms show progress, draft and abandonment behaviors are declared, and the submission defines a success target and HTTP method.

rules.description: form-flow-spec.json must exist with form_id (string), fields (array), and submission (object). Forms without a spec cannot be validated.
Every field with required:true must declare at least one validation rule. Required fields without validation rules silently accept invalid input.
Every entry in the serverErrors array must have a code (string) and userMessage (string). Server errors without user messages show raw technical codes to users.
When a form has more than one step, every step must declare progressIndicator:true or the spec must declare globalProgressIndicator:true. Users cannot gauge completion without progress context.
When draftEnabled:true, draftSaveTrigger must be auto or manual. Auto-save and manual-save have different UX implications and must be explicit.
When draftEnabled:true, draftStorageKey must be a non-empty string. Without a storage key, drafts from different form contexts will overwrite each other.
submission must declare redirectTo or onSuccess. A form with no defined success behavior leaves users on the form with no feedback.
Multi-step forms must declare abandonedBehavior as save-draft, discard, or warn-then-discard. Without a policy, navigating away causes silent data loss.
Every field must declare both id and type. Fields without ids cannot be referenced by validation errors or server mappings.
submission.method must be POST, PUT, or PATCH. Forms without an explicit HTTP method default unpredictably across frameworks.
